title: Supreme Court Hears a Big Case About Climate Change
summary:
On Monday, the U.S. Supreme Court listened to arguments in an important case about climate change.

Leaders in Boulder, Colorado, are suing two energy companies, Suncor and ExxonMobil. Boulder says climate change causes natural disasters that cost the city money. It wants the companies to help pay. Boulder also says the companies were not honest about oil and gas.

The companies say they are not to blame. Their lawyer, Kannon Shanmugam, said more than two dozen cases like this are going on around the country. The companies say these cases could cost billions of dollars.

Only eight of the nine justices heard the case. Justice Samuel Alito stepped aside because he owns stock in oil and gas companies. If the vote is a 4-4 tie, an earlier Colorado ruling that let Boulder's case go forward will stay in place.

Expert Amy Howe said it was hard to tell how the court will decide. A decision may not come until early next year.
why_it_matters: The court's decision could affect who pays when climate change damages the places where kids and families live.

keywords.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States.
Arguments are the reasons lawyers give to convince judges.
Climate change is the long-term warming of Earth's weather patterns.
Suing means asking a court to make someone pay for harm or fix a problem.
Justices are the judges on the Supreme Court.
A ruling is a decision made by a court.
